title: Torus fixed flags and a separating dominant one-parameter action
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T$, a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, its unipotent radical $V$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ and the quotient $Q=G/B$ with right torsor $\pi:G\to Q$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on characters by $(w\chi)(t)=\chi(n^{-1}tn)$ for a representative $n$ of $w$. The scheme $Q$ is smooth, projective and connected. It admits a $G$-equivariant closed immersion $Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ for a finite-dimensional rational $G$-representation $E$; a rational representation is a group-scheme morphism to $\operatorname{GL}(E)$, and $\mathbf P(E)$ parametrizes lines. For any representatives $n_w\in N_G(T)(F)$, the fixed subscheme $Q^T$ (the functor of points fixed by $T$ after every algebra extension) is the finite disjoint union of the reduced points $e_w=n_wB$, indexed without repetition by $W$. The $T$-weights on the tangent space $T_{e_w}Q$ are exactly $\Phi\setminus w\Phi^+$, each with multiplicity one, where $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup(-\Phi^+)$. There is a cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ such that $\mathbf P(E)^{\lambda(\mathbf G_m)}=\mathbf P(E)^T$ as fixed subschemes; the pairing is specified by $\alpha\circ\lambda(t)=t^{\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle}$. In particular $Q^{\lambda(\mathbf G_m)}=Q^T$. The empty-root case is included.

source.place: Theorem 4.27 (a subgroup as a line stabilizer), Theorem 17.9 and Section 18c; Summary 21.41, Lemma 13.51 and the paragraphs before Proposition 21.70, pp.436,446; tangent-space calculation in the proof of Theorem 21.73, p.447. Fixed-subscheme smoothness for torus actions is Theorem 13.1; the roots of the tangent quotient are characters, valid also in positive characteristic.

proof.text: The quotient and torsor in the hypotheses satisfy the quotient condition of [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry]: two lifts have the same image precisely when their ratio lies in $B$, and the faithfully flat torsor supplies local lifts. Apply that node with $H=B$. It gives that $Q$ is smooth, geometrically integral, proper and Noetherian, and that $\pi$ is smooth. In particular $Q$ is connected. Here $B$ is smooth and connected by its Borel definition, so this application has no inseparable-stabilizer exception.

Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-scheme-line-stabilizer] to $B\subset G$, obtaining $(E,D)$ with stabilizer exactly $B$ on every test algebra. The orbit map $g\mapsto gD$ is invariant under right $B$. Its values on the torsor kernel pair agree; [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] therefore gives a $G$-equivariant map $i:Q\to\mathbf P(E)$. This is a monomorphism: for two test-scheme points with equal images choose common fpqc-local lifts $g,h$ to $G$; equality of lines implies $g^{-1}h\in B$, whence equality in $Q$, and descent detects that equality globally. Projective space is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $Q$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $i$ proper; [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes it a closed immersion. Choosing a basis of nonzero $E$ identifies its projective space of lines with an ordinary projective space, proving projectivity of $Q$.

source.place: Theorem 4.27 and the paragraph preceding Proposition 21.70; Stacks Tags 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), 01W6 (lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed), 04XV (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion)

proof.text: Choose $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to its first factor on $E$. Each resulting eigenspace is stable under the other factors: their actions commute, so applying another factor to $t^av$ again gives $t^a$ times that vector. Apply the same node to the second factor on each eigenspace, and continue for the finite number $r$ of factors. This gives $E=\bigoplus_{\chi\in S}E_\chi$ for a finite set $S$ of distinct characters, with an eigenbasis. These are group-scheme identities on all test algebras. For $r=0$ this is the single trivial weight (since $E\ne0$). Let $U_i=Q\cap D_+(x_i)$ for this eigenbasis. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] these are affine opens covering $Q$, and $T$ preserves them because it multiplies each $x_i$ by a character. On $D_+(x_i)$, its action on the point-coordinate $u_j=x_j/x_i$ is multiplication by $\chi_j\chi_i^{-1}$. Thus the fixed subfunctor is the closed subscheme obtained by setting $u_j=0$ whenever $\chi_j\ne\chi_i$: in the Laurent polynomial coaction equation $(\chi_j\chi_i^{-1}-1)u_j=0$, distinct monomials have coefficients $u_j$ and $-u_j$. The same equations on $U_i$ agree on overlaps and represent $Q^T$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, Remark 12.13 and the proof of Lemma 13.51; standard affine projective charts

proof.text: For any $q\in Q(F)$ the fibre of $\pi$ is nonempty and smooth by [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry]. By [lem-pc-dense-separable-points] it has a point with residue field finite separable over $F$, hence an $F$-point. Write $q=gB$. Its scheme stabilizer is $gBg^{-1}$ by the torsor identity; consequently it is fixed by $T$ exactly when $T\subset gBg^{-1}$. In that case [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-borel-transitivity] gives $n\in N_G(T)(F)$ with $nBn^{-1}=gBg^{-1}$. Then $n^{-1}g$ normalizes $B$, so lies in $B$ by [lem-sfb-borel-scheme-normalizer]; hence $q=nB$. Conversely every $nB$ with $n\in N_G(T)(F)$ is fixed. For injectivity, if $a\in N_G(T)(F)\cap B(F)$, apply the projection $p:B\to T$ from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] to $ata^{-1}$, after arbitrary scalar extension. Since $ata^{-1}\in T$ and $T$ is commutative, $ata^{-1}=p(a)t p(a)^{-1}=t$. Thus $a\in C_G(T)(F)=T(F)$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer]. The cosets $e_w$ are therefore indexed without repetition by $W$. This group is finite by [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections].

source.place: Proposition 17.53, Summary 21.41 and the paragraphs preceding Proposition 21.70

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak g=T_1G$ and $\mathfrak b=T_1B$, with tangent spaces defined by [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. The differential of $\pi$ at $1$ is surjective: given a dual-number tangent vector to $Q$ at $B$, regard $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ as an $\mathcal O_{Q,B}$-algebra; formal smoothness of $\mathcal O_{G,1}$ over that stalk, supplied by [lem-sfb-smooth-stalk-formally-smooth], lifts the residue map $\mathcal O_{G,1}\to F$. This lift gives the required tangent vector to $G$ at $1$. The kernel consists precisely of the dual-number points in the fibre $B$, so is $\mathfrak b$. At $e_w$, apply the same argument to $g\mapsto gn_wB$, whose fibre at $1$ is $n_wBn_w^{-1}$. This map intertwines conjugation by $T$ on $G$ with the left action on $Q$, since $tgn_wB=(tgt^{-1})n_wB$. Hence it identifies $T_{e_w}Q$ with $\mathfrak g/\operatorname{Ad}(n_w)\mathfrak b$ as a $T$-representation. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha$, each root summand one-dimensional. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $\mathfrak b$ contains exactly the positive-root summands and $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$. Conjugation by $n_w$ carries weight $\alpha$ to $w\alpha$ because $t(n_wvn_w^{-1})=n_w((n_w^{-1}tn_w)v)n_w^{-1}$. Taking the quotient leaves exactly $\Phi\setminus w\Phi^+$, each once. This uses characters, never differentials of characters.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 21.73, tangent quotient at w0, with the same quotient calculation at any w; Stacks Tags 02H6 and 0B2C

proof.text: Each $U_i$ of step 3 is affine, finite type and smooth over $F$. Its represented closed fixed subscheme is smooth by [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth], so these opens make $Q^T$ smooth. Apply [lem-pc-dense-separable-points] to $Q^T$: its rational points are dense because $F$ is algebraically closed. By step 4 those points are a finite list. Each is closed (on an affine neighbourhood its residue map to $F$ has maximal kernel), so their finite union is closed and dense, and equals the entire underlying space. Every point is therefore open and closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], its local ring is regular of dimension zero; the defining regularity condition says its maximal ideal has zero generators, so the local ring is a field. Its residue field is $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. A singleton open scheme has an affine neighbourhood equal to itself and thus is $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Hence $Q^T=\coprod_{w\in W}\{e_w\}$ as schemes, including reducedness.

source.place: Theorem 13.1, Proposition 17.53 and the finite-constant assertion preceding Proposition 21.70; Stacks Tag 056S

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] choose a regular $\lambda_0$ with $B=P(\lambda_0)$. Comparing its Lie description with the positive-root summands in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ gives $\langle\alpha,\lambda_0\rangle>0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$. Identify $X_*(T)$ with $\mathbf Z^r$ using $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ be the coordinate cocharacters. For a positive integer $N$ put $\lambda(N)=N^{r+1}\lambda_0+\sum_{i=1}^rN^i e_i$. For each positive root its pairing with this cocharacter is a polynomial in $N$ with positive leading coefficient, so is positive for all sufficiently large $N$. For each distinct $\chi,\psi\in S$, its pairing with $\chi-\psi$ is a nonzero polynomial: the coordinate coefficients $\langle\chi-\psi,e_i\rangle$ are not all zero and occur in different degrees below $r+1$. Such a polynomial has only finitely many integer roots. Choose $N$ large enough for all inequalities and outside all these finite sets. Then $\lambda=\lambda(N)$ is dominant and separates all distinct weights of $E$. If $\Phi$ is empty there are no positivity inequalities. If $r=0$, there are no distinct weights, and $\lambda=0$ already works.

source.place: Lemma 13.51 and the dominant-chamber choice preceding Proposition 21.70

proof.text: On every eigenbasis chart $D_+(x_i)$ from step 3, the fixed scheme for $\lambda$ is cut out by $u_j=0$ whenever $\langle\chi_j-\chi_i,\lambda\rangle\ne0$. Indeed, invariance is the identity $(z^{\langle\chi_j-\chi_i,\lambda\rangle}-1)u_j=0$ in $A[z,z^{-1}]$, whose coefficients force $u_j=0$ for a nonzero exponent over any test algebra $A$. This remains true when that integer is divisible by the characteristic. Separation makes this exactly the condition $\chi_j\ne\chi_i$, so its fixed ideal equals the torus fixed ideal on every chart. Thus $\mathbf P(E)^{\lambda(\mathbf G_m)}=\mathbf P(E)^T$ as schemes. Finally, because $i:Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ is equivariant and a monomorphism, a test-scheme point of $Q$ is fixed precisely when its image is fixed, after every algebra extension. Pulling back the two equal fixed subfunctors proves $Q^{\lambda(\mathbf G_m)}=Q^T$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q59-290418729 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all eight steps against the statements of the 20 cited nodes and Milne iAG2017: Lemma 13.51, the paragraph before Prop 21.70, and Prop 17.53. There are no new nodes. The statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged from live, where the item is still unsplit, and no cited node depends on the item. Step by step: (1) Borel quotient: smooth, proper and geometrically integral. (2) Line-stabilizer orbit map descended along the fpqc cover π; it is a monomorphism by common lifts, then proper over separated, then a closed immersion. (3) Factor-by-factor weight basis and chart equations (χ_jχ_i^{-1}−1)u_j=0. (4) Transitivity plus the Borel normalizer give the fixed points nB; injectivity holds because p:B→T forces the element to centralize T, hence lie in T; W is finite. (5) dπ is surjective by formal smoothness of the stalk with kernel 𝔟, the convention (wχ)(t)=χ(n^{-1}tn) is verified, and the weights are Φ∖wΦ⁺, each once. (6) Fixed-scheme smoothness on the affine U_i plus density of rational points give a finite discrete scheme with regular 0-dimensional local rings, so Q^T=⊔Spec F. (7) B=P(λ₀) and λ(N)=N^{r+1}λ₀+ΣN^i e_i is dominant and separating. (8) z^m−1 with m≠0 forces u_j=0 in every characteristic, so equivariance and the monomorphism give Q^λ=Q^T. Small cases checked: G=T, SL₂ weights ∓α at e and e_s, repeated weights, p dividing the exponent. Batch-5: all five flagged citations reach sec-trace-formula only through the Mathlib leaves lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent and lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement. These are generic algebra/descent facts, not given by the trace-formula or Poincaré assumptions, so they are accepted. The worker-written tool_uses (standard charts, dense separable points, smooth⇒regular) are generic tools and accepted. Minor: independence of e_w from the representative is not written, but it is one line from T⊂B. lem-sfb-general-flag-isolated-linear-action (N6) is weaker and more general, not a duplicate. No SGA source is used.
